title: The Four Costs That Matter
gist: Gave revisits a four-cost framework (capital, labor, energy, government) for comparing major economies, noting the US cost of capital currently runs roughly 350-400bp above China's.

insights.claim: Gavekal periodically re-applies a four-cost framework from Louis-Vincent Gave and Charles Gave's 2013 book Too Different For Comfort — comparing the cost of capital, cost of labor, cost of energy and cost of government across major economies — while acknowledging the exercise is often subjective.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: Investors comparing country allocations can use this four-lever framework (capital, labor, energy, government cost) as a structured lens, though the authors flag it as inherently subjective rather than precise.
insights.quote: In 2013, in a book entitled Too Different For Comfort, Charles and I attempted to look at the major economies through the prism of four important costs: the cost of capital, the cost of labor, the cost of energy and the cost of government.
insights.locator: In 2013, in a book entitled Too Different For Comfort

insights.claim: Of the four costs, cost of capital is the easiest to compare across countries because it can be read directly off short rates, long rates and the shape of yield curves.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: Yield-curve comparisons remain the most tractable cross-country signal in this framework, useful as a quick relative-value check versus the harder-to-quantify labor, energy and government cost components.
insights.quote: Comparing and contrasting the cost of capital between different countries is undeniably the easiest task of the four.
insights.locator: Comparing and contrasting the cost of capital between different countries

insights.claim: As of September 2026, the cost of capital in the US is roughly 350-400 basis points more expensive than in China.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: A ~350-400bp US-China cost-of-capital gap underscores a persistent funding-cost advantage for China, relevant to relative equity/credit valuation and carry-trade positioning between the two economies.
insights.quote: For example, today, the cost of capital in the US is roughly 350bp to 400bp more expensive than it is in China.
